text:
alex: Heads-up — hit an edgecase in the new starter app: JSON streaming + tool (function) calls. Model returned two top-level JSON docs separated by a newline and the SDK parser crashed. Onboard demo died when we hit that prompt.

alex: example output from the model:
```
{"op":"get_user","id":123}
{"op":"error","msg":"not_found"}
```

alex: stacktrace was inside sdk/jsonparser.js when it tried JSON.parse on the full stream.

mira: Ugh, yeah that's the classic multi-document stream problem. Our JS SDK still assumes single-root JSON for json_mode. We added a tolerant parser in python last quarter but never shipped the parity fix to the JS helper.

sam: I ran into a similar thing but with auth retry — when the client does automatic retry after a 401, the helper re-encodes the function call payload and ends up double-encoding the body for the tool plugin. Repro in starter-kit using the OAuth flow.

kim: Quick workaround: configure json_mode: "multi_document" (experimental) on the client so the parser splits on newlines and parses each doc separately. In JS: 
```js
const client = new Redwood({ json_mode: 'multi_document' });
```
In python it's: 
```py
client = RedwoodClient(json_mode='multi_document')
```
This avoids blowing up but it's not ideal for schema validation.

mira: Right — multi_document helps parse but breaks our strict schema validation because we currently validate only the first doc against the declared schema. We need the SDK to validate each doc in order or return a structured error listing which doc failed.

alex: Filed a quick issue with a repro and logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/starter-kit/issues/2145 — includes a tiny condensing sample that hits the multi-doc case.

devex-bot: Created issue #2145 in redwood-inference/starter-kit and linked PR template.

sam: repro command I used locally: 
```bash
curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @multi_doc_prompt.json | jq -c .
```
multi_doc_prompt.json contains a prompt that instructs the model to emit two separate json objects.

kim: Proposed short-term plan: (1) ship parity patch for JS parser to mirror python tolerant behavior, (2) add a json_mode: "validate_all" that runs schema validation per-doc and emits an array of results, (3) add a test in starter-kit that exercises auth-retry + stream to catch double-encode regressions.

mira: 👍 I'll pick up the JS parser change. alex — can you attach the minimal prompt and the failing request id so I can write unit tests?

alex: attaching prompt in the issue now and pasting the failing request id there. Thanks — appreciate the quick triage.

sam: thanks, team — this was blocking an internal demo so happy to help QA once there's a branch. :thumbsup:

kim: adding a note: when we do the validate_all behavior, we should keep a small opt-in flag initially so we don't break folks relying on current single-doc semantics.

mira: agreed. I'll open a draft PR against the JS SDK and tag you all.

alex: cool — closing the loop here. If anyone sees other streaming/fncall oddities plz drop them in the issue.
